name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2183: The hunt economy check reads the tail of control_app.log, and that log carries item names an AI read off his game screenshots. Both of its patterns were plain substring searches, which a review turned into two concrete attacks. A name containing the words CONSOLE BOOT would move the window past every real hunt line, so a live runaway would be reported as no hunt has run, and because the check own failure message also names the marker, a log that ever quoted it would blind the check permanently. Separately, a line merely containing the phrase hunt done with new sightings for 0 name counted as a PASS, and two empty passes is exactly the trigger, so one honest miss plus one unlucky item name would be reported as the loop. Both patterns are now anchored to the start of a line and to the full shape only the emitter writes, the boot marker including its version and pid. Three more from the same review. A spend that cannot be attributed to the running build is now unknown rather than a confident missing, because without a boot marker the window may be entirely from before the fix, which is precisely the reading that made this check wrong on his machine in the first place. A single pass of any size used to return ok, so one pass costing 3434 reads and finding nothing was filed as a miss rather than a loop, and there is now a bar for that pinned from both sides so it can never sit above its own signal: several times one honest pass of 144 reads, and well below the largest spend ever observed. Six cases are pinned including the two original behaviours, which is the half that matters most, because scoping a window is the easiest way to blind a check while making it look more precise.
